• 2-3+ years of experience in AAA or indie game development 

• Proficiency in tools like Blender, Maya, 3ds Max, Substance 3D Painter and Photoshop.

• Strong eye for composition, color theory, scale, proportion, architecture, and environmental storytelling.

• Portfolio showcasing game-ready environments.

Benefits

• Competitive Salary.

• Dynamic, multicultural and fun environment.

• You will be working for the world's leading provider of game services.

• We empower our people and offer regular progression opportunities to ensure our employees flourish.

Side (formerly PTW) is a global video game development and services provider, offering technical and creative solutions to many of the largest developers and studios around the world. “Billy Rides the Bus” is a 24-page picture-book manuscript (plus a short section of supporting educational material) created for children aged 3 to 7. The story introduces first-time riders to the school-bus experience while gently reinforcing key safety rules. 

What I need now are full-colour illustrations—bright, simple, cartoon-style drawings with bold, inviting shapes—that make Billy and his friends instantly likeable and easy to recognise in future titles. Warmth, accuracy, and consistency matter: every spread must clearly show the real proportions of a typical yellow school bus, its surroundings, and the safe behaviours the children model. 

Collaboration is central to this project. I will provide reference photos, page-by-page art notes, and prompt feedback so each revision moves us closer to a cohesive visual identity that can carry through the entire series. 

Deliverables 
• 24 finished story illustrations, plus front cover, back cover, and endpaper design 
• 2-3 spot images for the educational section 
• Layered, print-ready files (CMYK, 300 dpi) and web-optimised versions 
• Character turnaround sheets for Billy and core friends to keep future books visually consistent 
• Up to two rounds of revisions per spread to fine-tune details and ensure safety steps are shown correctly 

Final acceptance hinges on the artwork being both engaging for the target age group and technically accurate in depicting: waiting at the bus stop, boarding and riding, and crossing close to the bus—elements that will appear across the series. 

If you love bringing friendly characters to life and are comfortable refining work through constructive feedback, this project sets the foundation for a long-term collaboration on the rest of the Billy Rides the Bus series.

full:
Design RF IOT Modules for WiSUN for India / North America - project needs the schematic capture and PCB layout, in Altium Designer, of a low-cost Wi-SUN FAN 1.1 sub-GHz radio module for smart meters. 

The module is a re-spin of the existing EFR32FG25 module onto the larger-memory, OFDM-capable EFR32FG25B222F1920IM56, with a maximum transmit power of +16 dBm from the SoC's integrated PA. 

There is no external PA, and no additional power supply: the module runs from the host 3.3 V rail.

The module keeps the existing outline, 29-pad LGA footprint and host pin-out, so it is drop-in compatible with existing hosts. Two band variants are built from one PCB, selected by fitted RF components:

India: 865–868 MHz.
North America and Paraguay: 902–928 MHz (one common design).

Scope of Work
In scope

Altium Designer project set-up from the Customer's existing projects and templates.

Schematic capture for both band variants, using Altium's Variant Manager for the band-specific parts.

Component selection and library work (schematic symbols, footprints, 3D models, parameters).

RF circuit design: balun, harmonic low-pass filter and RX matching starting values for 865–868 MHz and 902–928 MHz, from the reference design and Silicon Labs guidance.

PCB placement and routing, including RF, crystal, DC-DC and decoupling layout.
Design rule set-up, ERC and DRC clean-up, and the manufacturing output package.

Three design reviews with the Customer (schematic, placement, routing).

One post-prototype ECO round: component value changes from the Customer's RF tuning, and small layout fixes (Section 9).

full:
Hiring an Art Director for a mobile 2D isometric strategy game teaching Chola / Chozha dynasty history (c. 985-1070 CE) for ages 10-14. India-first launch, freemium, built on Defold.

**Before the full spike we need test samples we can drop into our Defold build.** Shortlisted candidates are paid a small fee to produce samples; the winning sample extends to a £1,500-£2,500 spike, and the spike extends to a 3-4 month full production contract (~500 sprites).

**Samples we need (approx. 1-2 days of work):**

1. One isometric building sprite — paddy field hut, tier 1, 256×192 px, PNG RGBA, transparent background, pivot bottom-centre.
2. One unit idle animation — spearman, 4 frames, 128×128 px each, PNG RGBA, pivot feet-centre.
3. One-paragraph style note explaining your technique choice (hand-drawn, 3D-rendered-to-2D, or hybrid) and one primary historical source you referenced (bronze, relief, or inscription).

**Visual direction (locked):** historically realistic, 2:1 isometric, period-accurate armour and buildings referenced from Chola bronzes and temple reliefs (Brihadisvara, Gangaikondacholisvarar). Not stylised, not chibi. Child-appropriate — no blood, no gore, no civilian battlefield characters, no sexualised armour, no caricature.

**Hard constraints:**
- Original work only. No reference from Clash of Clans / Lords Mobile / Rise of Kingdoms / Age of Empires Mobile.
- AI for moodboard only. **No AI-generated art ships.**
- Every delivered sprite must pass a historian review and a child-safety review.

One addition to the sample delivery. Because historical accuracy is a hard release gate on our side, we also need to see your working process alongside the final PNGs. **This applies equally to every shortlisted candidate.** Please include the following with the sample ZIP:

**1. Source file (your native format).**

Deliver the editable working file you used to produce the sprites. One of:

- **Blender:** `.blend` with the model, rig, lighting, and camera preserved. If you used a hybrid workflow with 2D touchup, include the touchup source too.
- **Photoshop:** `.psd` with **all layers preserved, unflattened**. Named layers preferred.
- **Procreate:** `.procreate` file (includes native time-lapse — good, keep it).
- **Krita / Clip Studio / Affinity Photo:** native format with layers preserved.

A flat 2-layer PSD at 2048×2048 downscaled is not a working file; it's an export. We need the real one.

**2. Short process recording.**

A **30-60 second screen recording** of any touchup pass on one frame — early sketch, cleanup, colour pass, shading — whichever moment best shows your workflow. Any of these is fine:

- Procreate time-lapse export (the built-in one is perfect — turn it on before you start)
- OBS / QuickTime / Loom screen capture while you work
- A short Instagram-reel-style over-the-shoulder phone recording of your iPad/tablet

Narration is welcome but not required. Upload unlisted to YouTube / Vimeo / Loom and send the link. Purpose: we want to see your decision-making process, not a polished presentation.

**3. 15-minute call with our historian.**

Once the sample ZIP arrives, we schedule a short **Google Meet or Zoom** with our historian reviewer. They'll ask you to walk through the primary source you cited — which specific bronze or temple relief, what you drew from it, what you changed and why. Comes with the territory because every shipped sprite will need historian sign-off; this is the first one. Please share **three 30-minute windows in your calendar over the next 7 working days** so we can match a slot.

**Why we ask:** our brief commits every shipped sprite to a named primary source (bronze, relief, inscription). Reviewing the working file, the process recording, and your source walkthrough together is how we verify the citation is real rather than retrofitted. It's standard for us; please flag now if any of the three is a problem on your end.

Everything else from the previous sample spec stands.

**In your bid, include:**
1. 2-3 portfolio links to shipped mobile 2D game art.
2. Your proposed technique and why.
3. Days to produce the sample set.
4. **One specific question you have about the direction after reading this post.** Bids without a specific question are not shortlisted.

desc: Title: 3D Costume Artist: Modular Uniform Cuff Trim & Morph Calibration (Fan Art Project) Pipeline: Blender + Daz Studio 4.24 (Genesis 9) Upfront Verification (Required to Be Considered) To be considered for this project, you must include a screenshot from inside Daz Studio 4.24 …
full:
Title: 3D Costume Artist: Modular Uniform Cuff Trim & Morph Calibration (Fan Art Project)

Pipeline: Blender + Daz Studio 4.24 (Genesis 9)

Upfront Verification (Required to Be Considered)
To be considered for this project, you must include a screenshot from inside Daz Studio 4.24 with your proposal showing work relevant to this milestone—specifically a Genesis 9 clothing/accessory asset in the viewport with the Parameters pane (showing custom fitting/adjustment morph sliders), Scene pane (showing rigged Wearable Presets/Smoothing Modifier), or Morph Loader Pro visible. Proposals without a Daz Studio screenshot will not be considered.

Project Overview
Five sleeve rank trim assets (01–05) are already modeled, UV-mapped, textured for Iray, and rigged for Genesis 9, currently shaped to a straight cylindrical sleeve. My live dForce uniform dress has a subtle forearm taper and a slight flare at the hemmed cuff, causing the existing trims to clip into the fabric.

The goal of this project is to conform the resting geometry of all 5 trims to the live dress mesh and add clean, non-destructive fitting morphs in Daz Studio 4.24 so they sit cleanly during posing and dForce simulation.

Files Provided
Source .blend file containing the 5 rank trim variations.

Existing 5 Genesis 9 .duf Wearable Presets (01–05) along with their data folder and 4K PBR/Iray texture maps.

Dress_Live_Fit_Ref.obj — Reference export of the live dForce uniform dress (DAZ Studio 1 unit = 1cm scale) showing the exact forearm taper and cuff flare.

Scope of Work & Technical Requirements
Conform Resting Geometry to Live Dress Mesh

Reshape/conform the resting cuffs of all 5 rank trim variations in Blender to follow the exact forearm taper and cuff flare of Dress_Live_Fit_Ref.obj.

Leave a clean, even resting clearance over the sleeve surface with zero clipping.

Important: Preserve the crisp woven bullion thread thickness and silhouette—do not use a blanket inflation/Push deformation that bloats the individual cords.

Add Fitting Morph Sliders (via Morph Loader Pro)

Export morph targets from Blender (maintaining exact vertex order) and import them into Daz Studio 4.24 via Morph Loader Pro for all 5 presets, saved cleanly as morph assets in the data folder:

Expand Cuff (Radial) (Required): Expands the trim rings radially outward from the forearm axis by up to ~3–5 mm to clear dForce folds or different character forearm shapes, without inflating thread thickness or sliding the trim down the arm.

Slide Forearm (Up / Down) (Required): Shifts the trim cleanly up or down along the forearm axis (approx. ±1–1.5 cm) to accommodate minor sleeve pull during posing.

Flare Cuff (Recommended): Subtly flares the wrist-side edge outward relative to the upper edge to accommodate wider cuff draping during dForce simulations.

Daz Studio 4.24 Rigging, Smoothing & File Hygiene

Keep all existing Genesis 9 rigging, auto-follow compatibility, UV maps, and Iray materials intact.

Add a Smoothing Modifier to each trim (defaulting to low Smoothing Iterations 1–2 and moderate Collision Iterations 3–5, so it can track minor dress surface changes without softening the fine woven detail).

Maintain a clean, portable Daz content directory structure (data/ + Wearable Presets) with relative texture paths and no absolute local file paths.

Final Deliverables & Verification
5 updated .duf Wearable Presets (01–05) verified in Daz Studio 4.24 + updated data folder (including the new morph .dsf files).

Updated source .blend file containing the conformed resting meshes and shape keys.

Verification screenshots from Daz Studio 4.24 showing:

Zero clipping against Dress_Live_Fit_Ref.obj in resting A-pose.

Clean deformation with the Genesis 9 elbow bent (~45°–90°).

The new Expand Cuff and Slide Forearm morph sliders visible in the Parameters pane and functioning cleanly.

full:
Project: "Der Weingärtner" (working title) – a vineyard management sim (WISIM) for PC/Steam, built in Godot 4 by a solo developer.

Setting: A fictional wine village on the Neckar river in southern Germany, starting in 1985. The player runs a small family vineyard: pruning, tying, spraying, harvesting, selling grapes to the cooperative. The map shows the village, the farm, and the vineyard plots as isometric tiles. The look should be clean, colorful, and slightly retro – friendly and readable, not photorealistic.

WHAT I NEED (INITIAL PAID SET)
Vineyard ground tiles in three terrain types, each in four seasons:
1. Flat vineyard (rows on level ground)
2. Slope vineyard (rows running down a hillside)
3. Steep terrace vineyard (narrow terraces held by dry-stone walls, with small stone stairs between them – typical for the Neckar valley)

Seasons for each terrain type:
- Winter: bare, pruned vines, brown wood, canes bent onto the wire, bare or frosted ground
- Spring: first light-green shoots, buds breaking, some grass between rows
- Summer: full green canopy, small green grape clusters
- Autumn: yellow/orange leaves, ripe dark-blue grape clusters

= 12 tiles in total. If the price is too high, start with the slope vineyard in all four seasons (4 tiles) as a test.

PERIOD DETAILS (IMPORTANT)
The game is set in 1985 in a German wine region, so please avoid the modern / American vineyard look:
- Wooden posts (weathered, grey-brown) with wire trellis – no white metal or concrete posts
- No fences around the plots; borders are a narrow dirt/grass path, a low stone wall or simply the next plot
- Rows close together (narrow-track tractors fit between them)
- Grass strips between the rows are fine but no modern drip irrigation

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
- Isometric projection 2:1 (e.g., 128×64 px base diamond; vines and posts may extend above, so canvas e.g., 128×128). Open to your suggestion for the best size – please tell me what you'd recommend.
- Tiles must connect seamlessly to neighboring tiles of the same type (rows continue across tile borders).
- Rows always run in the same direction on all tiles.
- Consistent light direction (top-left) and a consistent limited palette across all seasons so they can be swapped without the map "jumping."
- Must stay readable when zoomed out: The player should recognize the season and terrain type at a glance.
- Transparent PNG exports + layered source files (PSD, Krita or Aseprite).
- Please keep posts/wires, vines, grapes and ground on separate layers. Later I want to show states such as "posts broken," "harvested" or "overgrown" by changing single layers.

LICENSE
- Full commercial rights for use in the game trailers store page and marketing.
- Exclusive: The tiles must not be resold as stock assets.
- Credit in-game credits is of course offered.
- Hand-made art only please (no AI-generated images) – required for Steam store disclosure.

POSSIBLE FOLLOW-UP WORK
If the test goes well there will be more work over months:
1. Additional vineyard states like harvested damaged posts frost damage overgrown neglected newly planted.
2. Farm and village buildings like farmhouse barn wine cellar town hall cooperative church etc.
3. Small characters vehicles like grape pickers narrow vineyard tractor trailer etc.
4. Character portraits for family members event messages UI icons tools diesel wire posts grapes money etc.

I need a Unity environment / technical artist to build a playable London map that will ship as the core location for our game, followed by two DLC expansions that extend the city with new districts and interior scenes. The visual direction blends “Realistic modern London” with touches of a “Stylized or cartoon-like London,” so assets must capture real-world landmarks while retaining a slightly exaggerated, colourful charm.

We’re seeking an experienced freelancer or small team to create a new, playable London environment from scratch to game built in Unity.

We are collecting project quotations, estimated timelines and milestone proposals. This is a fresh environment production project, not a repair assignment.

The job moves through three milestones: 
1. London . 
2. DLC 1— map expansion 
3. DLC 2— map expansion

The core playable map covers approximately 3.6 km², including the River Thames. We can provide geographic boundaries, reference material and our agreed visual direction.
We also want separate quotations for two future DLC map expansions, with their boundaries and sizes agreed during scoping.

Scope
- Model geographically accurate London streets, buildings and recognizable landmarks, including Landmarks.
- Create complete building exteriors: facades, roofs, corners, entrances, doors and windows.
- Build roads, pavements, junctions, railways, bridges, riverbanks and terrain.
- Add authentic British road markings, signs, traffic lights, street furniture and vegetation.
- Produce finished textures, materials and lighting that follow one consistent art direction.
- Add varied window treatments and convincing simulated interiors behind non-enterable windows.

We want real London architecture and proportions translated into a cohesive, premium stylized visual language.
Our graphic and texture reference is the POLY – Paris European City asset pack. The reference guides material treatment, detail and visual finish; the architecture and setting must remain British

The quoted scope must include modelling, UV mapping, texturing, materials and in-engine presentation.

Quality expectations

Each milestone must be visually inspected and technically checked before delivery. Buildings must have complete roofs and surfaces, clean joins, correctly fitted openings and believable placement.
Delivered areas must be free of known holes, unintended overlaps, flickering surfaces, floating objects and blocked routes.

Deliverables
- One integrated, playable London map.
- Fully textured Unity scenes, prefabs, materials and assets.
- Editable modelling and texture source files.
- Two separately scoped DLC expansion packages.
- Asset licence inventory and handover documentation.
- Optimization and profiling evidence against agreed reference hardware.

full:
Project Brief: Bilingual Editorial Website & Online Shop

**Overview**
I am looking to bring my floral and creative studio online with a bilingual (**English / Spanish**) website that feels like an art-directed digital publication rather than a standard agency template. The experience should be pared-back, photography-driven, and luxuriously spacious—defined by generous negative space, expressive typographic hierarchies, and fluid transitions that let our botanical work breathe.

**Visual & Aesthetic Reference**
For layout pacing, typography, and minimalist restraint, see: `[https://tulipstudio.hr/en](https://tulipstudio.hr/en)`

**Core Objective**
To present our studio, bespoke floral services, and curated shop with quiet confidence and clarity. Visitors should seamlessly switch between English and Spanish and move effortlessly from our brand story into our services, online shop, press features, and inquiry flow.

**Site Architecture & Navigation**

* **Global Header:** Minimalist navigation bar featuring our logo, an **EN / ES language switcher**, and the exact 5 main menu items:
1. **Shop** *(Tienda)* – Streamlined e-commerce storefront to purchase physical floral goods/objects directly (with cart, checkout, and shipping), plus a short inquiry form for bespoke/custom orders.
2. **Services** *(Servicios)* – Editorial presentation of our signature offerings (e.g., *The Flower Bar – Interactive Floral Experiences for Celebrations*), structured with refined copy, process notes, high-res photography, and a direct booking/inquiry trigger.
3. **Contact** *(Contacto)* – Streamlined inquiry form for events and custom requests, alongside direct contact details, location, and social links.
4. **Studio** *(Estudio)* – Our brand narrative, creative philosophy, and behind-the-scenes/team imagery.
5. **Publicity** *(Publicidad)* – Clean editorial archive of press clippings, interviews, and media features.

*(Note: The **Home** page should act as an editorial entry point introducing the brand statement, full-bleed hero imagery, and curated previews leading into Services, Shop, and Studio.)*

**Design & Interaction Requirements**

* **Editorial Layout:** Full-bleed photography, sharp edges (no rounded corners or heavy drop shadows), asymmetric grids, and strong contrast between large editorial serif headings and crisp, understated sans-serif body copy.
* **Color Palette:** Warm, restrained minimalism (off-white/cream grounds, soft charcoal typography, and subtle brand accents) that gives every visual element breathing room.
* **Motion & Micro-interactions:** Smooth inertial scrolling, seamless page-to-page transitions, subtle image reveal animations, and refined hover states (GSAP, Barba.js, or native equivalent).
* **Responsive & Performance-First:** Tailored breakpoints for large desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile. Lightweight asset handling (WebP/AVIF, lazy loading) and multi-language SEO structure (`hreflang`, localized meta tags).

**Tech Stack & CMS Preferences**
I am platform-agnostic, provided the backend is intuitive enough for non-technical team members to manage **both English and Spanish content**, swap imagery, publish press features, and handle shop inventory/orders (e.g., Webflow + Localization & E-commerce, Framer, Craft CMS, or a custom headless setup like Next.js/Astro + Sanity/Shopify). Clean, modular, and well-documented code is a must.

**Deliverables**

1. Fully functional, responsive bilingual website (EN/ES) deployed to our custom domain with SSL.
2. Configured CMS & E-commerce backend, accompanied by a short Loom walkthrough for day-to-day content and order management.
3. Digital style guide documenting typography scales, color tokens, and component spacing rules.
4. Complete handover package: source files/repository, custom code snippets, and animation/transition documentation.

**How to Apply**
Please share **1–2 live links** that demonstrate your ability to balance strict minimalism with fluid, tactile motion, along with your **recommended tech stack** (specifically addressing bilingual + e-commerce handling), **estimated timeline**, and **ballpark investment**. If this aesthetic and scope resonate with you, let’s create something timeless.

full:
AI pipeline: apply a tile from a raw photo onto existing stair images using masks (no 3D rendering)
We make stairs clad with porcelain/ceramic tiles. We have about 42 stair images (different designs and angles). We do NOT want to render the tile in Blender. We need an AI pipeline that puts the tile onto our existing stair images, using masks.
Input:
A raw, real-life tile photo. It is not cropped or scanned: shot at an angle, uneven light, reflections, background, low resolution.
Base stair images (~42), plus masks for each surface: treads, risers and nosings/edges. If needed, we can also export extra passes from Blender: UV, depth, normal, object/material ID.
What the AI must do:
Extract the tile from the photo: find it, fix the perspective, crop it, and remove glare, shadows and noise.
Recreate the tile in high quality while keeping it identical to the original: same pattern, veining, structure and colour distribution. No reinterpretation.
Apply the tile inside the masks with correct perspective, real-world scale (e.g. 60×120 cm), realistic tile layout and grout lines, and correct cuts on treads, risers and nosings.
Keep the stair geometry, edges, lighting, shadows and reflections of the base image. The result must look like a real photo of the stairs.
Process all ~42 images automatically for each new tile.
Key requirement:
The tile face must be exactly the same across all ~42 images. It's the same tile, not 42 variations. The pattern must not change or drift between images. Colour can be fine-tuned on our side; the tile face is the priority.
Deliverables:
A working tool I can run myself: ComfyUI workflow or Python script, local or API-based. Input = tile photo; output = 42 finished images.
Documentation and a handover session.
Acceptance test on 5 of our real tile photos.
Ideal candidate:
Strong ComfyUI / Stable Diffusion / Flux experience: ControlNet, IP-Adapter, inpainting, relighting, upscaling
Texture projection/warping onto masked surfaces using UV or depth
Portfolio showing AI that preserves product details (product placement, material swaps, interior visualization)
In your proposal, please include:
Your approach: how will you keep the tile pattern identical across all images and avoid AI hallucination?
Relevant examples (material swap / product-preserving work)
Timeline, budget and hardware requirements

full:
OVERVIEW
We are building a synthetic human face dataset in Blender using the open-source Google GNM parametric head extension:
https://www.reddit.com/r/blender/comments/1uzaxc3/google_gnm_open_source_parametric_head_released/

Please note: We will not be sending pre-made .blend files upfront. You can download and install the free Google GNM Blender extension directly and build all materials, eye shaders, hair, and accessories around the standard GNM head setup. Everything you deliver must plug cleanly and easily into our existing Google GNM Blender workflow.

Our goal is to use an automated Python rendering pipeline to randomize face shapes, skin profiles, hairstyles, facial hair, glasses, and headwear—generating diverse synthetic human portraits (similar in variety and framing to Microsoft’s FaceSynthetics dataset: https://github.com/microsoft/FaceSynthetics/blob/main/docs/img/dataset_samples.jpg), rendered to match real Near-Infrared (NIR) camera imagery.

Target IR Output & Eyeball References:
- Sample IR Face Output: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11263-021-01432-4
- High-Resolution NIR Eye & Iris Reference: https://www.researchgate.net/figure/High-resolution-NIR-face-images-and-corresponding-face-and-iris-images-a-High_fig1_221383633

(These links—along with additional sample IR images we will share with you—serve as our visual target. We will iterate together on your initial sample renders to fine-tune the look so it closely matches our actual camera output.)

We are looking for an experienced Blender look-dev / character artist to deliver:
1. An IR-accurate skin, eye, and mouth material library tailored to the Google GNM head.
2. A modular library of hair and accessories that fit cleanly across Google GNM head variations.
3. A calibrated lighting/render setup inside Blender that reproduces real NIR image characteristics.

------------------------------------------------------------

1. IR-ACCURATE SKIN, EYE & MOUTH MATERIAL LIBRARY
- IR Skin Tones & Ages: Distinct skin profiles covering very fair to very deep tones (referencing the Monk Skin Tone Scale) plus age variations (smoother skin for younger faces, fine lines/pores/sunspots for older faces), calibrated specifically for how melanin, subsurface scattering, and skin reflectance behave in monochrome Near-Infrared imagery.
- Close-Up Detail & Visible Skin Marks: High-resolution (2K minimum) PBR textures that hold up in tight portrait close-ups—ensuring pores, fine lines, and natural skin marks (moles, freckles, blemishes, scars, and light stubble shadow) remain clearly and accurately visible under IR illumination, with zero seams or stretching on the GNM head mesh.
- Script-Friendly Master Shader: A single master skin shader with clearly exposed, easy-to-script controls for skin tone/IR reflectance, roughness/shine, subsurface scattering, freckle/mole/blemish intensity, and stubble shadow, alongside pre-configured presets for all profiles.
- IR Eyeball & Iris Physics (Priority):
 * Eyeballs must accurately replicate real Near-Infrared optical behavior (matching the NIR eye reference link above):
 - Deep black pupil with a sharp white glint/dot (corneal specular reflection) when looking toward the camera.
 - Clearly defined grey iris with realistic iris pattern/texture and natural IR reflectance across different iris shades.
 - Bright white sclera with realistic wetness and a subtle tear line.
 * Natural IR-tuned materials for lips, eyebrows, eyelashes, and interior mouth parts (teeth, gums, tongue) on the GNM mesh.

------------------------------------------------------------

2. MODULAR ACCESSORY LIBRARY (COMPATIBLE WITH GOOGLE GNM HEADS)
We need a comprehensive library of modular, mix-and-match assets built at real-world scale with clean topology and PBR materials, designed to maximize visual variety and generate a wide range of unique synthetic combinations:
- Head Hair & Eyebrows: A wide variety of hairstyles (short, medium, long, straight, wavy, curly, coily, tied back, shaved/buzz, etc.) plus diverse eyebrow shapes and densities in multiple natural shades (including grey and white).
- Facial Hair: A broad selection of styles (light and heavy stubble, short beards, full beards, moustaches, goatees, sideburns, etc.) across multiple shades.
- Eyewear: A diverse collection of prescription glasses (thin metal, thick acetate, rimless, half-rim) with clear refractive lenses, alongside sunglasses (aviator, square, round, wrap-around, oversized) with tinted, gradient, and mirrored lenses that behave realistically in IR.
- Headwear & Face Coverings: A wide assortment of headwear options (caps, beanies, wide-brim hats, headscarves, turbans, hoods, etc.) plus various surgical and cloth face masks.

GNM Compatibility & Automation Requirements:
- Parametric Fit: Because Google GNM generates varying face shapes, head sizes, and expressions, accessories must adapt/fit cleanly to generated GNM heads with zero clipping or floating gaps (e.g., bound via surface/mesh deformers or rig/shape-key compatible setups so they follow head shape changes automatically).
- Clean Layering: Accessories must combine together (for example, wearing glasses, a cap, and a beard simultaneously) without intersecting each other.
- Automation-Ready Structure: Because we will randomize combinations via a Python script, all objects, collections, materials, and shader parameters must follow a strict, consistent naming convention and clean hierarchy.

------------------------------------------------------------

TECHNICAL & LICENSING REQUIREMENTS
- Built and tested in Blender (Cycles) using native Blender tools and the free Google GNM extension—no paid add-ons required to open or render.
- Textures saved with relative paths or packed cleanly into the .blend files.
- Usage Rights: All work must be original or properly licensed so we have unrestricted rights to use the 3D assets internally to generate and use synthetic 2D image datasets commercially.

The objective is to automate as much of our recruitment process as possible to improve 
recruiter productivity, reduce manual effort, speed up sourcing and bring greater efficiency to 
the overall recruitment cycle. 
We aim to build an AI-powered recruitment platform that integrates multiple job portals with 
our in-house ATS, and automates recruitment tracking and reporting. 

A. Centralised AI-Powered Job Search 
Develop a new search interface with Claude AI integrated at the backend, connecting to the 
following job portals: 
 Naukri 
 Shine 
 Indeed 
 LinkedIn 
The system should: 
1. Allow recruiters to search across multiple job portals from a single interface. 
2. Accept Job Descriptions (JDs), keywords, skills, experience, location and other 
relevant search criteria. 
3. Use AI to understand the JD and identify relevant candidate profiles. 
4. Display profiles ranked by their relevance to the requirement. 
5. Eliminate the need to individually visit and search each job portal.

B. Candidate Profile Display & Shortlisting 
The search interface should display candidate profiles in a list/summary format rather than 
automatically opening individual profiles. 
 Mobile numbers and contact details should not be visible in the search results. 
 Profiles should not open automatically. 
 Recruiters should be able to review basic candidate details and AI match scores. 
 Recruiters will manually open only the profiles they wish to shortlist. 
 Shortlisted profiles should then be added to our ats system recuitZ.
Integration nd automation
Automated MIS and weekly reporting

Core scope 
• Build or train an AI/ML routine (Python, Node, or comparable stack) that scans job boards, LinkedIn-style networks, GitHub, and other open sources to identify profiles matching a role description I feed it. 
• Extract key fields—name, headline, skills, location, email or alternative contact, and profile URL—and normalise them to Recruit’s data model. 
• Push the enriched records into Recruit in real time, handling duplicates gracefully. 
• Provide a simple dashboard or command-line report that shows the number of leads pulled, success/error logs, and API response codes for traceability. 

Deliverables 
Phase 1 AI-powered search interface and job portal integration 
Phase 2 Candidate shortlisting and SpotRecruit integration 
Phase 3 Automated MIS, dashboards and weekly reporting 
Phase 4 Process optimisation and additional AI-based automation 

Acceptance criteria 
• At least 80 % of captured profiles populate correctly in Recruit with no manual cleanup. 
• Duplicate detection works against existing candidate IDs or email addresses. 
• Runtime for a single search stays under 5 minutes for 1,000 profiles. 

When you respond, highlight relevant experience building similar sourcing bots, Recruit (or comparable ATS) integrations, and any AI/NLP models you have deployed in production.

About SweetSpot Heating & Cooling
SweetSpot is a growing home-services company in the New York metro, and we are building our creative team from zero. This is the number one creative seat in the company, not a slot in a large agency hierarchy. The strategist hired here owns the function, works directly with the owner, and has a real path to leading the team as we scale.
About the role
We are hiring a creative strategist who will own paid ad creative end to end: research, angles, hooks, scripts, briefing creators and editors, and the learnings that turn winners into the next batch.
This is not a "make pretty ads" role and it is not strategy-only. You will direct really strong video editors and UGC creators, and you will use AI (including Claude Code) as your production engine for research, hooks, scripts and variants. We are honest about the level this role is hired at: we are looking for strong raw talent with real direct-response instincts who wants ownership and serious training, and who wants to grow into a top-tier strategist with us. You will get mentorship, a proven creative system, and weekly learnings reviews. In return we expect pace, curiosity, and work you can defend.
What you will do
• Build the research base first: homeowner avatars, desires, objections, competitors, and our own ad account history. No angles before research.

• Plan concepts in a structured roadmap, each with angle, avatar, desire, mechanism, authority, awareness level, emotion, positioning and urgency.

• Write hooks and scripts built for the first 3 seconds: one desire, one avatar, one message per ad.

• Brief UGC creators and editors so clearly they can execute with no follow-up call, and review their work to a finished, launch-ready ad.

• Run the testing system: from one winning angle, build structured iterations where each variation tests something named.

• Run the learnings: label every ad (Breakthrough, Spend Winner, KPI Winner, Loser), state why it performed, and turn that into the next round.

• Hit 20 to 30 finished, launch-ready ads per month at full pace, working with our editors and AI workflows.

What we are looking for
• Direct-response ad experience: you have written ads that ran as paid social (Meta or TikTok) and you can show them.

• A testing system, not just good taste. You can explain how you turn one winner into 20 variations.

• Research discipline. Your hooks trace to evidence, not guesses.

• AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your creative workflow and can show how.

• Execution: you have briefed creators or managed editors and shipped finished ads.

• Ownership mindset: you talk about business outcomes, not just outputs delivered, and you close feedback loops: you learn, you apply, you show what changed.

• Local services or lead generation experience is a plus, not a requirement. Seasonal urgency, emergency calls, proof and trust are the game here.

Pay and structure
• Contract (1099), remote, month-to-month: $4,000 to $8,000 per month, 40 hours per week, based on experience.

• Performance bonus structure discussed after the trial month, tied to winning ads.

• Growth path: this seat grows into leading the creative team. One of the paths we model is editor or strategist to team lead as spend scales.

Our hiring process (exactly how it works)
• Short application: portfolio of ads you wrote that actually ran, plus 3 short answers (your testing system on a real winner; one ad you iterated and what it tested; your AI workflow).

• Interview 1 (30 minutes): screening and craft in one call, run as a working session on your past ads: what did you learn, how did you apply it, what feedback loops did you complete.

• Paid test: $100 flat, 48 hours, capped at 4 hours of work, paid regardless of outcome. A short research snapshot, hooks, scripts, an iteration plan and an execution plan for a real scenario.

• Interview 2 (final, with the owner): we walk your test together and you defend your choices. References are checked after this call (we will ask to speak with one past employer). Two interviews total, no more.

• Paid 30-day trial at your full agreed monthly rate, with daily contact, mentorship and a weekly check-in. Written decision at day 30.

We hire off the test and the trial, not the interview. If you are the kind of strategist who would rather prove it than pitch it, apply.

About us
At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

The role
Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.

You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.

You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

• Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list.

• Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

• Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs.

• Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.

• Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.

• Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.

• Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.

• Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.

• Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.

• Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.

• Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.

• Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.

Your background
You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through:
• A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there.

• Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with.

• Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working.

• A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role.

full:

About us
Convertibles is a CRO and Shopify development agency for 8 and 9 figure D2C brands. We've just brought Google and YouTube ads in-house under the same roof, run by our co-founder Clay. He's been doing Google Ads for ecommerce since 2013: built and exited his own brand on Google Ads and CRO, then ran Google and YouTube for brands spending $50k to $500k+ a month on Google alone. The ads book today is around seven brands across the US, UK, EU and Australia, and it's growing.
The role
This is an apprenticeship with a real job attached. You work directly with Clay (x @ecomclay), learn how he runs accounts, and within 90 days you're running the weekly cycle on your first accounts yourself.
The weekly cycle, concretely:
• Monday: pull last week's numbers (Google Ads platform side plus the client's attribution tool - Triple Whale, Converge or Northbeam), update the reporting workbook, write the client update, produce the actions list. Exact campaign, exact change, why.
• Through the week: make the changes, watch pacing, check feeds and Merchant Center, build new campaigns (Search, Shopping, PMax, YouTube / Demand Gen).
• Client calls: sit in first, then run them.
How we work, so you know what you're signing up for
• YouTube and Demand Gen are the main event, not a side channel. We take a brand's winning Meta ads, recut them for YouTube, and scale. Accounts have gone from YouTube at 6-12% of media mix to 13-22%, at a return that held for over a year.
• Attribution-tool numbers decide YouTube, not platform numbers. If you've only ever judged campaigns on what Google Ads says, you'll learn a different lens.
• Everything gets a number. "Performance improved" is not a finding. "NC-CPA went from £38 to £30 on the same spend" is.
• AI is part of the workflow. Reporting workbooks, data pulls and first drafts are built with Claude. You don't need to be a developer, but you need to be comfortable working this way.
• There's a dev, CRO, QA and design team behind the ads. When a landing page or a feed needs fixing, someone fixes it.
Who fits
• 2-4 years hands-on in Google Ads for ecommerce. Your hands on the account, not managing someone whose hands are.
• You've run Search, Shopping and PMax on real budgets (at least one account at $20k+/month). You've at least touched YouTube or Demand Gen and want to go deep on it.
• Comfortable in Google Sheets / Excel. You can look at eight weeks of campaign data and tell me what changed and why.
• You know what a Merchant Center disapproval is and how to fix it.
• You write clearly in English. You'll be writing to clients by week five.
• Curious, direct, not precious about being told you're wrong.
Not a fit: agency account managers who relay what the specialist did. Meta buyers who "also do Google". Anyone who needs the basics explained.
Hours
Full-time, 40h/wk. Your morning overlaps with Clay (he's UTC+8), your afternoon overlaps with UK/EU clients and the US East Coast. Flexible beyond that.
First 90 days
• Weeks 1-4: shadow. Pull the data, build the workbooks, sit on every call.
• Weeks 5-8: draft the Monday updates and actions lists for two accounts. Clay reviews before they go out.
• Weeks 9-12: own the weekly cycle and the check-in call on your first account.
Comp is reviewed at 90 days. The per-account bonus starts when you own an account.
What you get
Direct training from someone who's done this for 13 years, on his own money and then on clients'. A team behind you. A real path: run accounts, then lead the Google / YouTube lane.
How to apply
Keep it short. Answer the questions in the form with numbers, not adjectives. Shortlisted people do a paid 2-3 hour test task, then a call with Clay.

The role
Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.
This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. • Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up

• Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it

• Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work

• Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them

• Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does

• Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of

• Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting

• AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further

• Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others

• Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it

Backgrounds that tend to fit
• Growth PM at a data-heavy consumer company

• MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them

• Product Minded Data scientist or analyst who wants to ship, not just report

Why this is interesting
• Competitive, top-of-market compensation

• You're defining what a growth PM looks like in an AI-native company, there's no inherited playbook

• Personalised retention is where the industry is going and we're building it early

• Real ownership: a segmentation framework, a product surface, and a P&L lever, with a direct line to the founding team

Performance Creative Strategist and AI Producer

Remote | Full time | Paid 30-day working trial

Icarus Digital Marketing builds and scales direct-response ecommerce brands, including brands in difficult and restricted categories. We are hiring a hands-on performance creative operator to work directly with the owners on our internal portfolio of brands.

This is not a conventional graphic-design role. We need someone who understands why Meta ads convert and can personally turn that understanding into high-quality static and video creative using current AI production tools.

You may come from dropshipping, affiliate marketing, DTC, a performance agency, or a creative media-buying background. We care more about commercial judgment, production ability, speed, and proof of work than polished credentials.

The work

You will use and help improve our internal Creative Cockpit. It takes a brand from research and foundational strategy through campaign creation, production, review, and delivery. For each brand, the system holds brand assets and voice, customer language and audience psychology, pains and desires, necessary beliefs, competitor intelligence, awareness levels, angles, hooks, offer context, prior creative, winners, and performance signals.

Your job is to turn that intelligence into creative that can sell.

• Read campaign briefs, audience research, voice-of-customer material, and brand strategy documents.

• Decide what each batch should test and why.

• Source and analyse strong visual and structural references.

• Develop angles, hooks, scripts, concepts, storyboards, and landing-page direction.

• Personally produce static ads and short-form video ads.

• Use AI image, video, voice, and editing tools at a high level.

• Create meaningful variants without producing repetitive AI slop.

• Review work for persuasion, visual quality, brand fit, platform fit, and compliance.

• Refine weak generations rather than accepting the first output.

• Package approved assets for launch and document what each concept tests.

• Read results and use the learning to plan the next batch.

What you must be good at

• Direct-response advertising and Meta creative strategy

• Audience psychology and voice-of-customer interpretation

• Awareness levels, hooks, angles, mechanisms, objections, offers, and message-market fit

• Understanding when an ad should lead to a PDP, advertorial, listicle, quiz, or sales page

• Static ad, UGC, and short-form video production

• Visual-reference analysis and controlled recreation

• Current AI image and video workflows using tools such as Seedance, Google Flow/Omni, Nano Banana/Gemini, GPT Image, Higgsfield, Kling, Sora, Veo, or comparable tools

• Editing, compositing, pacing, captions, sound, and final polish

• Fast, organised batch production

• Reading creative performance and choosing the next test

You are probably not right for this role if

• Your portfolio is mostly branding, organic social content, or attractive design without performance context.

• You call every asset “scroll-stopping” but cannot explain the audience belief or conversion mechanism.

• You are a strategist who depends on other people to make the work.

• You are a tool operator who needs someone else to provide every hook, angle, script, and decision.

• You use one prompt, accept the first output, and call it AI production.

• You cannot show exactly what you personally contributed to portfolio examples.

• You dislike volume, iteration, testing, or direct feedback.

What success looks like

Within 30 days, you can understand our strategy packs and operating system, take a structured brief from research to finished assets with limited supervision, produce a useful weekly mix of static and video concepts, explain the reason for every important decision, maintain quality while moving quickly, and suggest practical improvements to the workflow.

Compensation

The role begins with a fully paid 30-day working trial at USD $2,000. If the fit is strong, it becomes a long-term full-time position expected to pay USD $2,000 to $3,000 per month, based on demonstrated level, with additional performance upside available for an exceptional long-term operator.

We care about ability, English comprehension, reliability, some overlap with our working hours, and quality of output.

How to apply

Do not send a generic cover letter. Message Simon on WhatsApp at +353 86 349 5073 and begin with: I make the work.

• Send three Meta ads you personally made or materially directed.

• For each example, state exactly what you did and explain the audience, angle, hook, and intended next step in the funnel.

• Share any useful performance context you are permitted to disclose. Redacted evidence is acceptable.

• Show one weak or failed creative and explain what you learned or changed.

• List the AI tools you use in real production and explain your normal workflow from reference to finished asset.

• Send a Loom of no more than five minutes. Choose one Meta ad you respect, explain why it works, and describe the next three variants you would test.

• State your location, timezone, availability, and expected monthly compensation after the trial.

Applications without the requested evidence will not be reviewed. Shortlisted candidates will complete a small paid practical exercise before the 30-day trial.
